name: Text actions
definition: Use a button for an action. Quiet actions have no persistent border or underline; content links keep their prose treatment.
keyboard: Native Enter/Space; busy prevents resubmission without changing the label.
followUp: Retired link-btn throughout the room. Remaining raw markup is bounded in legacy-controls.json and uses shared CSS.

name: Icon actions
definition: Familiar glyph, accessible name, fast tooltip and stable target. Ambiguous commitments retain text.
keyboard: Tab and Enter/Space. No hover-only actions.
followUp: Use 14–16px glyphs in 24/28px targets; coarse pointers get 44px targets.

name: Metadata actions
definition: Counts and secondary actions wrap independently of a story title. Passive counts never look pressed.
keyboard: Ordinary Tab order; actions never nest inside the content-opening control.
followUp: Continue migrating raw metadata actions when changing item renderers.

name: Navigation links
definition: A destination has href and current-page semantics, without a prose underline. Navigation remains distinguishable by placement and hover/focus.
keyboard: Native link keyboard and context menu; intercept navigation only when the app handles that destination.
followUp: Docs contents uses uiNavLink; remaining outline and search rows use the same contract locally.

name: Content links
definition: Underlined references belong within reading content, citations and explanatory prose. Never remove underlines globally from anchors.
keyboard: Native links; destination text describes where they go.
followUp: Preserve article and documentation links; no fake button styled as a prose link.

name: Tabs
definition: Switch local panels; do not represent global destinations or preference values. Keep every panel mounted to retain reading state.
keyboard: One tab stop; Left/Right, Home/End, manual Enter/Space activation. Tab then reaches the panel.
followUp: Comparison uses real tab semantics at narrow widths and named regions in its side-by-side overview. Vertical and closable tabs are not supported yet.

name: Segmented choices
definition: A short mutually exclusive value set uses a labelled native radio group; selection does not mean opening a tab panel.
keyboard: Native radio arrows and Space; the label is the full target.
followUp: Audience selection uses the shared native radio group; product copy explains the visibility consequences.

name: Layout choices
definition: Persistent layout preference shown as compact preview cards in Settings. Exactly one active option, stable preview and text.
keyboard: Native buttons expose pressed state; changing a preview persists the preference.
followUp: Keep previews product-owned; migrate to a reusable choice-card binder when a second use appears.

name: Status and tag pills
definition: Passive metadata; never a focus stop. Meaning is written in text, not communicated by color alone.
keyboard: No keyboard interaction. Do not attach click handlers or required tooltips.
followUp: New marks and clip tags use uiBadge. Avoid adding a status pill where existing text already explains the state.

name: Selectable pills
definition: Interactive pill with a constant label and checkmark that reserves its width; use for selection or toggled filters.
keyboard: Native button with aria-pressed, Enter/Space; 24px floor and 44px coarse target.
followUp: Evidence selection uses uiChip. A future removable filter needs a separately named remove action, never a nested button.

name: Disclosures and accordions
definition: Native details/summary with one consistent chevron, target and text scale. Optional groups may allow many sections or only one open.
keyboard: Native Enter/Space. Do not add redundant aria-expanded or a focus trap.
followUp: Library filters, collection setup, watches, imports, reader outline, docs and Space sections use the shared disclosure.

name: Text and search fields
definition: Native text/search inputs with associated label, hint and error. A placeholder never substitutes for a name.
keyboard: Native editing and form submission. Error description belongs to its field.
followUp: All dynamic room input, select and textarea creation uses uiControl; uiField adds associated labels, hints and errors without overriding product search timing.

name: Textarea and select
definition: Native multiline and selection controls use the same field frame, label, error and minimum height.
keyboard: Native text/option navigation. Use a select for longer value sets.
followUp: Do not replace native selects with custom menus; a searchable combobox needs its own tested behavior.

name: Checkboxes and toggles
definition: An independent binary preference uses a named native checkbox. Its label is clickable and the value remains visible.
keyboard: Space toggles; ordinary Tab order.
followUp: Account listing and composer checkboxes remain local markup; migrate on change. Do not add a switch merely for visual variety.

name: Action menus
definition: Short list of actions in a native popover. Forms and rich content are not menus.
keyboard: Arrows, Home/End, first letter; Escape returns focus, Tab leaves, outside click dismisses.
followUp: Shared for global More and Room options. A context-menu variant is not implemented; do not label arbitrary popovers role=menu.

name: Dialogs and drawers
definition: Modal task surface with a name, explicit close, contained focus and restoration. Drawer is its edge-aligned placement variant.
keyboard: Native modal Escape and wrapped Tab; return to the opener.
followUp: Settings uses drawer. A nonmodal inspector must not reuse modal semantics without a separate focus contract.

name: Inline panels and rich popovers
definition: Forms and optional tools disclosed alongside their owning control. Use group/dialog semantics according to behavior, not a menu just because it floats.
keyboard: Trigger exposes expanded and controls; keyboard users can enter and leave; Escape restores a sensible focus target.
followUp: Quick reblog uses uiPopover and native audience radios. Reader tools remain inline groups with their existing selection lifecycle; they do not float or claim modal/menu semantics.

name: Selection trays
definition: Compact contextual actions in document flow, visible only with a selection. No extra heading is required when the count and actions explain it.
keyboard: Normal Tab order; clearing restores focus to material instead of losing it with the tray.
followUp: Evidence selection uses uiTray. Floating passage selection stays a specialized product composition.

name: Tooltips
definition: Short hint supplements a familiar control name; it cannot contain essential settings, errors or interactive content.
keyboard: 150ms pointer delay; immediate keyboard; Escape dismisses before parent overlay; hoverable content.
followUp: Touch actions work directly. Do not use tooltips on passive badges to hide essential meaning.

name: Toolbars and settings rows
definition: Compact wrapping action groups and labelled value rows. Expose a group name without adding unnecessary visible labels.
keyboard: Ordinary Tab order. Do not use role=toolbar without its composite keyboard contract.
followUp: Product toolbars may arrange shared controls; fields and controls own their validation.

name: Cards and list items
definition: Semantic content container with separate heading, metadata and actions; do not make a whole card a button containing other buttons.
keyboard: Content opener and secondary actions are independent focus targets.
followUp: Utility cards are shared. Seven reading forms remain intentional editorial product variants.

name: Pagination and load more
definition: Previous/next names its destination; numbered navigation exposes current page; incremental loading is an action.
keyboard: Ordinary Tab order. Preserve reading position and focus after adding content.
followUp: Document pager is shared; lane navigation and incremental reading retain local layout and tested scroll behavior.

name: Breadcrumbs and back navigation
definition: Back acts on the remembered reader stack. A breadcrumb is a location hierarchy, not decorative separator text.
keyboard: Back is a button; future clickable ancestors need a named nav/list and current-page semantics.
followUp: Current docs trail is informational. Do not add extra crumb labels to the room header.

name: Document content
definition: Comfortable reading scale separated from compact application controls, shared by articles and docs.
keyboard: Headings support focus destinations; find and passage controls have visible keyboard paths.
followUp: Shared module includes paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, media captions, code, tables and callouts. Product owns fetching and reading position.

name: Document navigation
definition: Contents, current page, on-page outline, search and pager surround readable content. Narrow contents disclose without losing the current page.
keyboard: Named nav regions, current-page announcement, Escape from contents, focus the loaded title.
followUp: Composed from shared links/disclosures/pager; docs-specific fetching and layout remain local.

name: Code and data tables
definition: Code scrolls inside its container; language and copy action stay outside selectable text. Data tables retain native headers and cells.
keyboard: Copy is named; scrollable tables are keyboard reachable and named.
followUp: No sortable data grid is shipped. Sorting, column resizing and virtualized rows need a separate tested contract if introduced.

name: Feedback and notices
definition: Explain the state and an available next action; avoid generic empty banners and needless headings.
keyboard: Error uses alert, loading/success use status; recovery remains a real button.
followUp: Long-lived failures belong inline, not only in a toast. Warning content can use info until a tested warning variant is introduced.

name: Toasts
definition: Dismissible notices: polite confirmations, persistent alert errors. Form failures and recovery actions stay inline.
keyboard: Arrival never moves focus. Dismiss is a named button. Timers pause on focus, hover and document hiding; focus returns after keyboard dismissal.
followUp: One room adapter uses the shared stack: three visible, FIFO queue, duplicate suppression, 6–20 second confirmations and persistent errors. No action buttons beyond dismissal.

name: Skeletons and progress
definition: Loading shape is decorative; readable status or aria-busy explains work. Determinate progress exposes value and maximum.
keyboard: Do not create focus stops. Honor reduced motion and accessible progress naming.
followUp: Catch-up uses real values. Loading feedback uses indeterminate native progress and readable status; room skeletons are static and hidden from assistive technology.

name: Avatars and media
definition: Images support content rather than replace names. Decorative avatars use empty alt beside the name; meaningful figures have text alternatives.
keyboard: An image is not interactive unless it has a named control wrapper.
followUp: Product image loading and editorial sizes stay local; avoid inventing an avatar size scale until used outside reading forms.

name: Dividers and spacing
definition: Use space before adding rules. Decorative separators carry no keyboard or announcement burden.
keyboard: No focus stop; use semantic hr only for a thematic break.
followUp: Existing separator is local CSS; all spacing must use the shared scale except intentional editorial geometry.

name: Composers and source pickers
definition: Product workflows compose fields, actions and feedback; draft text, validation and server state remain product responsibilities.
keyboard: Labels, submission prevention, error association and focus recovery are mandatory.
followUp: Several fields/actions still use local markup. They are recorded in legacy-controls.json; migrate per flow with behavioral tests.

name: Drag and resize
definition: Rearrangement must offer a non-drag route and retain other portals and saved material.
keyboard: Do not rely on dragging alone; tool-driven arrangement remains available.
followUp: No drag or resize handles are shipped. Room arrangement currently uses tools; lane controls navigate the layout. Require direct keyboard alternatives before adding handles.

name: Combobox and command palette
definition: Searchable option selection and command search have different keyboard and filtering requirements from action menus.
keyboard: Define active descendant or roving focus, Escape and selection semantics before building.
followUp: No current product control requires either. Add production use, a full contract and interaction tests before promoting to shared.

name: Tree and data grid
definition: Hierarchical selection and editable tabular data are composite widgets, not decorated lists or tables.
keyboard: Define the WAI-ARIA composite keyboard model before implementation.
followUp: Docs contents uses nested disclosures and links; it intentionally is not a tree widget. No grid need exists today.

name: Date and range inputs
definition: Prefer labelled native inputs when a product need arrives. A bespoke calendar or slider needs a concrete reason.
keyboard: Use native keyboard behavior and expose values/constraints.
followUp: No date grid or range widget is currently needed. Prefer a labelled native control when a real product need arrives.

name: Form submission and validation
definition: Native constraints and associated field messages for invalid input; server failures remain by the draft. Busy forms keep labels stable and reject duplicate submissions.
keyboard: Native Enter/submit and invalid-control focus; asynchronous errors announce without moving focus. Editing clears the field error.
followUp: Bind mutation forms with uiForm. Instant preference controls retain rollback in product code; live search retains its cancellation/generation checks.

name: File inputs
definition: Native file selection with an accessible name, shared field and selector-button tokens. Keep import errors and reports in the surrounding task.
keyboard: Native file dialog. A hidden OPML input is triggered by the visible named Import action; no custom keyboard model.
followUp: Account JSON upload, OPML import and catalogue use the native contract. No custom upload/drop-zone component is claimed.
